student.title: Present Perfect: Life Experiences
student.instructions: Read each section carefully. Work with a partner when you see speaking tasks. Write your answers on your own paper.

sections.label: Section A
sections.title: Key Words In Context
sections.instructions: Read the short definitions. Match each word from the word bank to the correct meaning. Write the word next to each number. Example: 0. not before now = never

items.prompt: before now, at any time in your life
not at any time in your life
by now; earlier than expected
up to now, in questions and negative sentences
something that has happened to you
in or to another country

sections.label: Section B
sections.title: Choose The Correct Form
sections.instructions: Choose the best answer for each sentence. Circle A, B, or C. Example: I have ______ finished my homework. A. ever B. already C. yet

items.prompt: Have you ______ been to a concert?
I have ______ tried skateboarding, so I want to try it.
She has ______ visited her cousin in another city.
We haven’t seen the new trailer ______.
Have you ______ met someone famous?

sections.label: Section C
sections.title: Build The Question
sections.instructions: Rewrite each prompt as a correct present perfect question or answer. Use the words in the prompt. Write one sentence for each item. Example: go / abroad / ever → Have you ever gone abroad?

items.prompt: you / ever / play / the guitar
he / already / finish / the project
they / never / travel / abroad
we / not / see / that movie / yet
she / ever / try / online gaming

sections.label: Section D
sections.title: Life Experience Survey
sections.instructions: Work with a partner. Ask and answer the questions out loud. Then write short notes about your partner. Example: Q: Have you ever been abroad? A: Yes, I have. I went to Japan last year.
sections.passage:
Mia: Have you ever been abroad?
Noah: Yes, I have. I visited my uncle in Canada.
Mia: Have you ever played in a school sports event?
Noah: No, I haven’t. I have never done that.
Mia: Have you already finished your homework?
Noah: Yes, I have already finished it.
Mia: Have you done your project yet?
Noah: Not yet.

items.prompt: Ask your partner about going abroad. Write one short note about the answer.
Ask your partner about a music experience. Write one short note about the answer.
Ask your partner about a sport or game experience. Write one short note about the answer.
Ask your partner about homework or a school task. Write one short note about the answer.
Write one follow-up question you asked or could ask.

teacher.overview: 60-minute B1 speaking lesson on present perfect life experiences. Students learn and practice ask/answer patterns with have/has + past participle, with controlled vocabulary support for ever, never, already, yet, experience, and abroad. The lesson moves from meaning and form to guided pair practice, then a speaking survey with follow-up questions. Main evidence is oral interaction; the worksheet supports accuracy, confidence, and vocabulary recall.
teacher.groupWorkGuidance: Use pair work throughout. With 24 students, form 12 fixed pairs for the controlled stages, then reorganize into new pairs for the survey so students speak with a different partner. Keep instructions short, model each task once, and use a clear stop signal such as 'Pens down, eyes up.' Circulate continuously, listening for target language and noting strong examples and common errors. Take brief feedback from 4-6 pairs, not the whole class. For mixed ability, pair stronger and weaker students when possible, but keep speaking turns balanced.

sections.label: Section A
sections.title: Key Words In Context
sections.explanation: These are the direct matches from the word bank. Check that students understand the meaning, not just the spelling.
commonErrors: Using 'abroad' to mean 'foreign' without the travel/country idea
corrections: ever = before now, at any time in your life
never = not at any time in your life
already = by now; earlier than expected
yet = up to now, usually in questions or negative sentences
experience = something that has happened to you
abroad = in or to another country
sections.teacherNotes: Quickly check pronunciation and concept. Use one simple spoken example for each word, then move on.

sections.label: Section B
sections.title: Choose The Correct Form
sections.explanation: Students choose the correct present perfect adverb based on meaning and sentence position.
commonErrors: Confusing 'Have you ever...?' with past simple
corrections: Affirmative completed action: I have already...
Negative unfinished action: I haven’t... yet
sections.teacherNotes: Have students explain why each choice fits. Briefly contrast 'ever' for questions and 'never' for negative personal experience.

sections.label: Section C
sections.title: Build The Question
answers: Have you ever played the guitar?
He has already finished the project.
We haven’t seen that movie yet.
Has she ever tried online gaming?
sections.explanation: Students rebuild the prompts into correct present perfect sentences. Accept standard subject-verb agreement and natural contractions.
expectedResponses: 1. Have you ever played the guitar?
2. He has already finished the project.
4. We haven’t seen that movie yet.
5. Has she ever tried online gaming?
commonErrors: Using past simple verbs instead of past participles
Putting yet in the wrong place
sections.teacherNotes: Accept 'Have you ever played guitar?' if the meaning is clear, but model the worksheet form with 'the guitar'.

sections.label: Section D
sections.title: Life Experience Survey
answers: Open speaking answers based on the partner's true responses.
Open speaking answers based on the partner's true responses.
Open speaking answers based on the partner's true responses.
Open speaking answers based on the partner's true responses.
Open speaking answer: one follow-up question such as 'When did you do it?' or 'What happened?'
sections.explanation: This is a pair speaking task. Students ask about experiences, listen, and write short notes. There is no single fixed answer because responses depend on the partner.
expectedResponses: For item 1: a short note such as 'Yes, went to Japan last summer' or 'No, never been abroad'
For item 2: a short note about music experience, such as 'Yes, been to a concert' or 'No, never played guitar'
For item 3: a short note about sport or game experience, such as 'Yes, played in a school match' or 'No, never joined a team'
For item 4: a short note about homework or a school task, such as 'Yes, already finished math homework' or 'No, not yet finished project'
For item 5: any sensible follow-up question linked to the partner's answer
commonErrors: Using past simple only: 'Did you go abroad?'
Forgetting to ask a follow-up question
Writing notes that do not match the spoken answer
corrections: Use the present perfect question form: Have you ever... ?
Use a short answer: Yes, I have. / No, I haven’t.
Add one detail if possible: when, where, or what happened
Ask a follow-up question to keep the conversation going
sections.teacherNotes: Listen for fluency, correct use of ever/never/already/yet, and follow-up questions. Encourage students to answer naturally and then expand with one extra detail.
